headline: Failed House bill would have created prison terms for spying on border agents for smugglers and for damaging border equipment.
what_it_does: The bill would have made it a federal crime to knowingly share the location or activities of law enforcement to help commit an immigration, customs, or drug crime, with up to 10 years in prison. It would also have set up to 10 years in prison for knowingly damaging or destroying devices used to control the border or ports of entry. It would have added tougher punishment for carrying or using a gun in connection with certain immigration crimes, such as helping a noncitizen with a felony conviction enter the US. The House voted it down on April 20, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: People who act as lookouts or 'spotters' for smuggling groups
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced up to 10 years in prison for passing along the location or movements of law enforcement to help immigration, customs, or drug crimes.
They would have faced up to 10 years in prison for knowingly damaging or destroying devices used to control the border or ports of entry.

who_it_affects.group: People who carry or use guns while committing certain immigration crimes
who_it_affects.how: They would have faced harsher sentences, for example when helping a noncitizen with a felony conviction get into the country.

who_it_affects.group: Federal border and law enforcement agencies
who_it_affects.how: They would have gained new criminal charges to use against people who interfere with border control.
